title: Backpressure and priority layers — signal fusion notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc explores a layered backpressure architecture that combines token-buckets, queue-depth limits and GPU utilization signals into a single admission controller. The goal is a low-latency, fair, and capacity-aware routing policy that works across regions and gracefully degrades under overload without manual sharding per-customer.

Context and motivation:
- Existing systems either rely purely on token-buckets (rate shaping) or queue-depth heuristics. Each alone misses important failure modes: token-buckets don't reflect sudden GPU saturation; queue depth alone can cause head-of-line blocking and unfairness.
- We need a compact control-plane decision that can be tuned per-customer/tier and also composed for multi-region routing.
- Constraints: keep serving runtime changes minimal, prefer controller-level heuristics, require observable signals for debugging.

High-level design overview:
1) Layered admission checks performed in order:
   - Fast local checks: soft token-bucket per-route + SLA-aware priority credit
   - Short-term queue filter: fast-path queue-depth limit with weighted admission
   - Slow path GPU check: sampled GPU-utilization signal fused with request cost estimate to reject or re-route
2) Signal fusion module in control plane aggregates: token-bucket deficit, queue depth percentile, per-GPU util, and request estimated tail-latency cost.
3) Router action types: admit-local, queue-delay (small backoff + retry), reroute-region, reject-with-backoff (429-like).

Admission algorithm (prose/pseudocode):
- Input signals: tb_credits(route), q_len(route), gpu_util(region), est_cost(req)
- Compute normalized signals:
    s_tb = clamp(tb_credits / tb_max, 0, 1)    // higher means more allowance
    s_q = 1 - clamp(q_len / q_thresh, 0, 1)    // higher when queue free
    s_gpu = 1 - clamp((gpu_util - gpu_target) / (1 - gpu_target), 0, 1) // higher when headroom
    s_cost = 1 - sigmoid((est_cost - cost_target) / cost_sigma)
- Weighted fusion score: score = w_tb*s_tb + w_q*s_q + w_gpu*s_gpu + w_cost*s_cost
- Admission decision:
    if score >= T_admit -> admit-local
    elif score >= T_delay -> enqueue-with-delay-hint (router issues small backoff token)
    elif region_has_capacity_alts -> reroute-to-best-region
    else -> reject-with-backoff

Notes on weights and thresholds:
- Default weights: {w_tb:0.35, w_q:0.25, w_gpu:0.25, w_cost:0.15} — tuned to favor token budget but still respect GPU headroom.
- Thresholds: T_admit=0.6, T_delay=0.35 (start conservative for safety).
- Per-tier config: enterprise customers get higher base tb_max and reduced effective est_cost.
- Dynamic adapt: controller should anneal thresholds down under prolonged overload.

Token-bucket specifics:
- Token buckets are per-route and per-organization (two-layer). Each request consumes tokens proportional to est_cost (non-linear; e.g., tokens = base_tokens * sqrt(seq_len/128)).
- Refill happens every 100ms to keep tight feedback.
- Overdraft allowed up to one refill window for burst smoothing; overdraft increases estimator penalty in fusion.

Queue-depth policy:
- Define fast path queue (in-proxy) and slow path buffer (centralized queue). Fast path queue limit is small (e.g., 64 requests) to keep p99 latency guarantees.
- When fast path is near threshold, router returns a delay-hint (ms) to clients or SDK for jittered retry. SDK will respect up to N concurrent inflight requests per route to prevent herd.
- Enqueue-with-delay will tag request with chosen timeout budget to avoid long-lived queue items consuming GPU cache.

GPU utilization signal and sampling:
- GPU util is noisy; avoid per-request blocking on util reads. Use exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) per-GPU and per-GPU-cluster, plus percentile signals (p50/p95 of util over last 30s).
- Calibrate gpu_target per machine-class (A100x2 vs L4 etc.). Region-level aggregated util is used for reroute decisions, node-level util is used for immediate rejection to avoid OOM.
- Sampled tail events (sudden spikes) trigger quick re-evaluation: if p95(util) > 0.92 for 15s -> escalate to emergency-throttle mode for that zone.

Multi-region routing and fallbacks:
- Router maintains region capacity score = fusion_score_region - network_penalty(region, client_loc).
- For reroute, pick best region with score >= T_admit_region. If none, try queue-delay; last resort reject.
- Cross-region reroute must respect data locality & privacy tags (per-customer). Config includes allowed_regions per org.

Fairness and isolation:
- Within a region, use deficit round-robin with priority lanes: "control" (platform internal), "enterprise", "standard", "free". Each lane has guaranteed min_tokens and share limits.
- Prevent starvation by occasionally sampling from lower-priority lanes when headroom present.

Observability and metrics to track:
- Per-route: tb_credits, tb_consumed_per_min, admission_rate(admit/delay/reroute/reject), queue_len, p50/p90/p99 latency post-admit.
- Per-region: gpu_util(p50/p95), region_admit_ratio, cross-region_reroutes, p99 tail loss due to rejection.
- Alerts: region_admit_ratio < 0.6 for >2min, p95(gpu_util)>0.9 for 30s, unexpected rejection spike (routes >> historical baseline).
- Traces: include admission_score breakdown (s_tb, s_q, s_gpu, s_cost) for every sampled request for offline tuning.

Runbook (quick):
- If region enters emergency-throttle: check p95 util, node OOM logs; if sustained, shift domain traffic to alternate region via control-plane override and increase T_admit for alts by +0.1.
- If token bucket underflowing for enterprise customers: validate refill heartbeat and check redis/keyowner lag; if keyowner lag>200ms, fail open for enterprise for 1min then escalate.

Testing and experiments:
- Local simulator that replays production traces and injects GPU spike events. Validate fairness across tenants and measure p99 latency under 2x and 5x load.
- Canary: enable fusion logic in read-only mode with scoring logged; then enable delay-path for 5% traffic, reroute for 1%, full admit/reject for 0.1% initially. Ramp to 25/5/1 respectively.
- A/B knobs: vary w_gpu from 0.1->0.5 to measure impact on tail latency and cost.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How much logic to push into data plane vs control plane? Currently prefer control-plane decisions with small proxy hints to minimize binary churn.
- Should token bucket estimation use ML-based cost estimator? Pros: more accurate; cons: complexity and cold-start fragility. Consider gated rollout for high-volume routes only.
- Retries: how to prevent retry storms on queue-delay? SDK cooperation needed; otherwise implement server-side jittered backoff window per client IP.

Action items:
- (Maya) prototype fusion module that emits per-request scores (2w).
- (Arjun) add GPU p95 sampling and EWMA pipeline (1w).
- (Lina) build queue-delay SDK contract and doc (1w).
- (Jonas) simulator + replay harness for canary tests (2w).

Appendix: quick example flow
- Client A sends request to region-us-east. Local tb_credits high (s_tb 0.9), q_len moderate (s_q 0.6), gpu_util p50=0.7 (s_gpu 0.3 after normalization), est_cost low (s_cost 0.9). score ~0.69 -> admit.
- Client B hits heavy model with est_cost high; tb low, q near threshold and gpu p95 spikes -> score 0.22 -> reroute to europe-west (if allowed) or reject-with-backoff.

This doc is intentionally practical: emphasizes observability and gradual rollout. Keeping the estimator simple initially will let us iterate based on real traces before adding ML-based components.

Notes to self:
- Keep profiling hooks in runtime to attribute per-request GPU kernels to request IDs to debug OOM/tail events.
- Avoid exposing raw GPU util numbers to user dashboards; surface only derived health signals.
